speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a child presenting with frequent nosebleeds, bleeding from your mouth or gums, and tiny red spots on your skin called petechiae. To understand what is causing this, have you been taking any new medicines or supplements lately?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: ITP (Immune Thrombocytopenic Purpura) is a strong possibility given the age and petechiae, but I must first rule out bleeding disorders like Hemophilia A or von Willebrand Disease. Have you noticed if these bleeds started suddenly after a minor injury or viral illness, or have they been present since birth? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count (CBC) with Platelet_Count. REQUEST TEST: Coagulation_Panel (PT, PTT, INR).
